findings.evidence: "This request timed out before it could finish."
findings.fix: Replace this entry's message with one that describes an actual empty-results state, and move the timeout message to its own error-state section.
findings.location: "Search results, no matches" section, first message entry (the one beginning "Message: This request timed out before it could finish.")
findings.violation: The section is titled "no matches," but this message describes a request timeout, a different failure than an empty result set, so it misrepresents what actually happened to the user.

findings.fix: Give this message its own trigger, such as "on-timeout," and add a suggested fix that offers a retry action.
findings.location: same entry, Fires and Suggested fix fields
findings.violation: A timeout happens some time after submission, not immediately, so listing the same "on-submit" trigger as the instant no-results message below it is misleading, and pairing it with "Suggested fix: none" leaves the user with no way to recover from the failure.

findings.evidence: "styled identically to informational banners elsewhere on the page, with no visual cue that this one demands action"
findings.fix: Specify a distinct visual treatment, such as an icon, color, or weight change, that marks this message as actionable rather than relying on the button alone.
findings.location: "Search results, no matches" section, second message entry (the one beginning "Message: No orders fall inside the selected date range..."), Signal field
findings.violation: The message asks the user to act, but the Signal field says its styling gives no indication that action is needed, and the listed Suggested fix, which only adds a button, does not resolve that styling gap.

findings.evidence: "Input on resubmission: not-applicable" beside a message that reads "Change the date range, or clear the filters to see every order."
findings.fix: Specify what happens to the date range and filter inputs when the user resubmits, instead of marking the field not applicable.
findings.location: same entry, Input on resubmission field
findings.violation: The message directs the user to change input and try again, so marking Input on resubmission as not applicable contradicts the resubmission behavior the message itself invites.

findings.evidence: "Placement: in the notification list, directly under the sync status row" versus "Signal: bold text at the top of the notification list, icon"
findings.fix: Pick one anchor for the message's position, either the sync status row or the top of the list, and remove the other.
findings.location: "Notification center, sync status" section, message entry, Placement and Signal fields
findings.violation: Placement anchors the message under the sync status row, while Signal places it at the top of the list; if the sync status row is not the first row, these describe two different positions for the same message.

findings.evidence: "so syncing does not spend a data allowance"
findings.fix: Reword to "so it does not use your data allowance."
findings.location: "Notification center, sync status" section, Message field
findings.violation: The phrase "spend a data allowance" is awkward and unclear about what resource is being conserved.
